sentences.text: This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .15,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 15.10.2022 at about 05.30 a.m., when petitioner was proceeding on left side of the road, Doddaianakatte Palya, Hebburu Hobali, Tumkuru Taluk,
Tumkuru in his TVS Excel 100 bearing Regn.No.KA-06- EW-5257, a Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-36-AX-7761, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against petitioner's vehicle resulting in accident.
Due to said accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter, petitioner was shifted to Govt. Hospital and later shifted to Siddaganga Hospital, Tumkuru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a huge amount towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as an Agriculture and milk vendor and earning a sum of .25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, 1st respondent did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further respondent No.2 admitted the aspect of issue policy bearing No.72150031220100020112 valid from 07.10.2022 to 06.10.2023 in respect of lorry bearing Regn.No.TN- 36-AX-7761 belonging to respondent No.1.
Further contended that the driver of said lorry did not have valid and effective driving license, fitness certificate and permit to drive the same on the date of accident.
Further contended that the petitioner was riding a two wheeler without having valid and effective driving license to drive the same.

Further contended that the alleged accident has taken place on 15.10.2022 and FIR has been filed by police after inordinate delay which clearly proves that the petitioner colluded with the respondent No.1.

Further the petition has not been filed within the stipulated period of 6 months and has been filed only on 17.07.2023, whereas the accident has taken place on 15.10.2022 and hence, this respondent is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 15.10.2022 at about 05.30 a.m., on the left side of the road Venkata Chalaiah vs Kaniraj A on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53389069/

sentences.text: 2 Doddaianakatte paly, Hebburu Hobali, Tumkuru Taluk, Tumkuru, due to the rash and negligent driving of lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-36-AX-7761 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

6. In order to prove case of petitioner, petitioner examined himself as PW.1, examined Dr.Ramesh,
working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.2, Manager in Medical Record Department at Hemavathi Hospital as PW.3 and MRD Executive in Medical Record Department at Siddaganga Hospital as PW.4 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P23 and closed his side evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the materials available on record.
8.

Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for  the following:-
 -:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 15.10.2022 at about 05.30 a.m., accident occurred while he was proceeding on the left side of the road at Doddaianakatte Palya, Hebburu Hobli,
Tumkuru Taluk, Tumkuru, due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-36-AX-7761 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10.
In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-36-AX-7761 by its driver, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver, the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross- examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited from PW.1 to disprove or disbelieve the case of petitioner.
In the cross examination, nothing to dispute or disbelieve the contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of driver of offending vehicle could be elicited from the witness.
Nothing to dispute or rebut the contention of petitioner related to the accident and cause of accident could be elicited during the cross examination.

11. Further, in order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of lorry by its driver, the petitioner produced Ex.P.15 First Information statement lodged by petitioner with the police on 15.10.2022.

On the basis of first information lodged by petitioner, the police registered the FIR as Venkata Chalaiah vs Kaniraj A on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53389069/
3 per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P2 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to vehicles are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The rear side of the offending vehicle is stated to have collided to the motorcycle driven by petitioner.
In the IMV report, the rear portion of offending vehicle is shown to have been damaged which aspect indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
The rider or owner of the offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages are caused to the vehicle.
The said document indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Ex.P.3 is the wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by the petitioner.
The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar which is marked as Ex.P.16.
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the factual aspects, as mentioned in the mahazar,
are contrary to the actual facts at the place of accident.
No materials are placed before the Tribunal to show that the actual facts at the place of accident differ from the facts mentioned in the mahazar.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the owner of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 338 of IPC as per Ex.P.5.

In the final report also,
the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioner could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove the case of petitioner.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver.

Under these circumstances,
relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.6,
this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Venkata Chalaiah vs Kaniraj A on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53389069/
4 Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-36-AX-7761 by its driver and same has resulted in injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.
In order to prove the injuries sustained, the petitioner produced Wound certificate issued by Siddaganga Hospital and Research Hospital, Bengaluru, which is marked at Ex.P.3.
The said document discloses that the petitioner sustained injuries and the injuries are grievous in nature.

So,
on perusal of records, the petitioner appears to have taken treatment at the hospital as an inpatient.

The petitioner produced Ex.P4 and P.6, Discharge Summaries, issued by Hemavathi Orthopaedic and Trauma Center, Bengaluru and Siddaganga Medical College & Research Institute and petitioner examined Dr.Ramesh, as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P18 & 19.

entities.text: Hemavathi Orthopaedic and Trauma Center, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: PW.2/doctor deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and stated that the petitioner has permanent physical disability of 85% of left lower limb and 42.5% to the whole body.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at Hospital.
The petitioner produced medical bills amounting to .4,71,372/- which are marked as Ex.P.7 and medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P8.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said documents.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also, nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .4,71,372/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 15.10.2022 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital as he sustained injuries.
During the time of treatment, the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner produced Ex.P.4 & 6 - Discharge Summaries, which disclose that the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 29.11.2022 to 16.12.2022, 09.09.2024 to 27.09.2024,
15.10.2022 and discharged on same day, 16.10.2022 to 11.11.2022, 11.11.2022 to 14.11.2022 and again from 17.11.2022 to 29.11.2022 i.e., for a period of 81 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 81 days to a sum of .40,500/-
appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.

(iv) Towards Conveyance:

sentences.text: The petitioner is the resident of Kalkere, Hebbur Hobli, Tumkur District and he got admitted to the hospital for availing treatment.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced Discharge Summaries marked at Ex.P.4 & 6.
The petitioner might have incurred expenses for conveyance during the period of treatment.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:
The petitioner contended that he was working as an Agriculture and Milk Vendor and was earning a sum of .25,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income, the petitioner not produced any satisfactory documents.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that he was earning .25,000/- per month, as contended by him.
No materials are placed by petitioner in order to substantiate his contention pertaining to his occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income of petitioner is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner considered as .15,500/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might not have attended his work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .30,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was admitted as an inpatient at hospital and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also examined Dr.Ramesh, working as an Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, and as PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.
The doctor deposed that petitioner sustained open fracture of distal femur and underwent internal fixation of femur.
PW.2 further deposed that the petitioner initially took treatment for internal fixation of femur and later for infection above knee amputation and then got discharged.

Further on recent examination,
petitioner complained of pain in left stump, difficulty to squat on floor, sit cross legged, to climb upstairs, walk on slope, stand on affected limb, difficulty to do routine activities.
Further on examination, petitioner is stated to be having restriction of joint movement of left hip above knee amputation left stump size 30 cm.
Further on radiological examination shows above knee amputation.
The doctor examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the permanent physical disability of 85% of left lower limb and to the whole body at 42.5%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.18 & 19 i.e., OPD Book and X-ray.
According to the petitioner he was working as an Agriculture and Milk Vendor and was aged about 65 years.
In order to do normal routine activities both lower limbs are very essential.
Both lower limbs are essential for performing daily activities.
But in the accident the petitioner has lost his left lower limb.

As the petitioner has lost his left lower limb, it is difficult for him to perform the activities as earlier and will not be Venkata Chalaiah vs Kaniraj A on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53389069/
6 unable to do the work as earlier.

sentences.text: Even if he uses an artificial limb, then also it may not be possible for him to perform his works as earlier.
So, it caused permanent working disability for him.
PW.2 doctor in his chief-examination deposed that above knee stump size is 30 cm measuring 16" (35").

As per Schedule I Part II of the Employees Compensation Act, at Srl.18 - Amputation below hip with stump exceeding [12.70 cms.] in length measured from tip of great trenchanter but not beyond middle thigh, percentage of earning capacity is 70.
By considering the age, occupation and injuries of the petitioner and evidence of doctors, the working disability of petitioner is considered as 70%.

The petitioner also examined Manager in Medical Record Department at Hemavathi Hospital,
Tumkuru as PW.3 and MRD Executive in Medical Record Department at Siddaganga Hospital examined as PW.4 and got marked documents at Ex.P20 to 23 i.e.,
authorization letter, case sheet and inpatient records.
In order to prove age, the petitioner produced Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card marked at Ex.P.14, wherein the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 01.03.1950.
The accident occurred on 15.10.2022.

As per the document furnished by petitioner,
his age appears to be 73 years as on the date of accident.
The respondents not furnished any materials in order to doubt the age of petitioner.
No materials are placed to rebut the document furnished by petitioner in order to prove his age.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the document furnished by petitioner is to be relied for ascertaining the age.

As per the document furnished by petitioner, his age was 73 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and last multiplier '05' is applicable to the present case as per Smt.Sarla Verma case.
As per ratio laid down in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay Kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

entities.text: Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay Kumar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Hem Raj V/s the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of a case, both the situations stand at the same footing.

entities.text: Hem Raj V/s the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of Pranaya Sethi and other Case the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that more than 60 years of age future prospects is not applicable.
Case on hand deceased was aged about 73 years and was receiving pension.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for future prospects.
The petitioner contended that he was working as an Agriculture and Milk Vendor and was earning a sum of .25,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income, the petitioner not produced any satisfactory documents.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that he was earning .25,000/- per month, as contended by him.
No materials are placed by petitioner in order to substantiate his contention pertaining to his occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the notional income of petitioner is to be taken into consideration.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner considered Venkata Chalaiah vs Kaniraj A on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53389069/
7 as .15,500/- per month.

Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Hence, the calculation of compensation as follows:
Annual Income before accident : (15,500/- x 12) .1,86,000/-
Loss of future earning p.a. (70% of prior annual income) .1,30,200/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 05 Loss of future earnings - (.1,30,200/- x 05) = .6,51,000/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .6,51,000/- under the head of permanent disability.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities :-
The petitioner lost left lower limb above knee and also he sustained open fracture of distal femur.
The petitioner also produced Ex.P.11 - Photographs to show injuries.
Hence, by considering injuries sustained by the petitioner, it is just and proper to award compensation of .50,000/- under the head deprivation of future amenities.

(viii) Towards Future Medical Expenses:
PW.2 in his chief examination has deposed that petitioner needs a prosthetics for amputated left lower limb.
The petitioner furnished estimation related to expense for prosthesis wherein it is mentioned about requirement of .5,50,000/- for future treatment.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case .1,50,000/-
appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future medical expenses.

14. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

15.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-36-AX-7761.
So, the respondents being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation amount of .14,52,872/-
(Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Fifty Two Thousand Eight Hundred and Seventy Two only)
with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.(future medical expenses shall not carry any interest)
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.

Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.

The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.

Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further the petition has not been filed within the stipulated period of 6 months and has been filed only on 17.07.2023, whereas the accident has taken place on 15.10.2022 and hence, this respondent is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

 -:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 15.10.2022 at about 05.30 a.m., accident occurred while he was proceeding on the left side of the road at Doddaianakatte Palya, Hebburu Hobli,
Tumkuru Taluk, Tumkuru, due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-36-AX-7761 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
11. Further, in order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of lorry by its driver, the petitioner produced Ex.P.15 First Information statement lodged by petitioner with the police on 15.10.2022.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the factual aspects, as mentioned in the mahazar,
are contrary to the actual facts at the place of accident.
No materials are placed before the Tribunal to show that the actual facts at the place of accident differ from the facts mentioned in the mahazar.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.
In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove the case of petitioner.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver.
The accident occurred on 15.10.2022.
As per the document furnished by petitioner,
his age appears to be 73 years as on the date of accident.
The respondents not furnished any materials in order to doubt the age of petitioner.
No materials are placed to rebut the document furnished by petitioner in order to prove his age.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the document furnished by petitioner is to be relied for ascertaining the age.
As per the document furnished by petitioner, his age was 73 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and last multiplier '05' is applicable to the present case as per Smt.Sarla Verma case.
In Hem Raj V/s the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of a case, both the situations stand at the same footing.
So, the respondents being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
